name: District of Columbia

creditorClaims.text: Claims are barred unless presented within 6 months after the date of first publication of notice of the appointment of a personal representative (D.C. Code § 20-903(a)(1)).

earliestClose.text: In unsupervised administration the personal representative closes the estate with a Certificate of Completion, which may not be filed before the time for filing creditors' claims has expired and after a 60-day objection period on the account sent to interested persons (D.C. Code § 20-735).

smallEstate.text: A small asset may be paid or delivered by affidavit of all known successors if the entire probate estate, less liens, does not exceed $40,000, includes no real property, and at least 60 days have passed since death (D.C. Code § 20-361; the online text includes temporary amendments expiring March 27, 2027).

simplified.text: Small estate administration in the Probate Division when the property subject to administration in D.C. is $80,000 or less (D.C. Code § 20-351, as amended by D.C. Law 25-302, effective March 21, 2025).

filingFee.text: Register of Wills fees are set by the Superior Court (D.C. Code § 15-707(a)); no fee for estates up to $500 and not more than $15 for estates up to $2,500 (§ 15-707(b)). The court's current fee schedule was not read.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (D.C. Code § 20-751), reviewable by the court using listed factors (D.C. Code § 20-753).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule: the court may review the reasonableness of compensation of an attorney employed by the personal representative, considering the work performed, estimates given, time spent and complexity (D.C. Code § 20-753).

uncertain: D.C. Superior Court Register of Wills fee schedule not read; filingFee.amount = null.
D.C. Code § 20-361 online text includes temporary legislation expiring March 27, 2027; effective date of the $40,000 affidavit limit not stated (smallEstate.effective = null).
